stem: According to the lesson, what makes chewed gum stretch instead of tear?

choices.text: It has been warmed and the sugar has been worked out of it
It has been chilled to firm up the resin
It has absorbed saliva and increased in volume

feedback: Correct. Warming softens the base and losing the sugar crystals is what changes the material. Re-study S-01.

stem: Which pair of changes does chewing make to gum before a bubble is possible?

choices.text: It cools the base and adds sugar
It warms the base and works the sugar out
It dries the base and hardens the resin

feedback: Correct. Those are the two changes named on S-01; a grainy feel means neither is finished.

stem: What does the lesson identify as the key to inflating the bubble once a pocket is open?

choices.text: Blowing as hard as possible to expand it quickly
Blowing steadily at an even pressure

feedback: Correct. Steady pressure, not force, is what S-02 calls the whole trick.
